title: Knowledge check: Measuring Application Performance

questions.prompt: Which principle best guides a correct implementation of measuring application performance?
options: Load multiple library copies and rely on whichever one executes last.
Measure before optimizing. Cache repeated selections, batch DOM updates, delegate events when appropriate, cancel stale requests, and avoid unnecessary layout reads or animation work.
Skip error handling and assume the default browser state is always correct.
Render user-controlled strings as HTML so the browser can infer their meaning.
questions.answer_key: Measure before optimizing. Cache repeated selections, batch DOM updates, delegate events when appropriate, cancel stale requests, and avoid unnecessary layout reads or animation work.
questions.explanation: Measure before optimizing. Cache repeated selections, batch DOM updates, delegate events when appropriate, cancel stale requests, and avoid unnecessary layout reads or animation work. Apply this principle with the API/version documentation linked in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which check is most useful after trying browser performance tools?
options: Use a removed jQuery API as the default for new code.
Assume the first attempt succeeded and skip verification.
Use browser performance tools deliberately, then inspect the actual DOM, request, or event result.
Bind another global handler after every render without cleanup.
questions.answer_key: Use browser performance tools deliberately, then inspect the actual DOM, request, or event result.
questions.explanation: A focused observation checks behavior rather than assuming the method call guarantees the intended result. Include an edge case when the state or inputs can vary.

questions.prompt: Which verification approach best supports professional work with measuring application performance?
options: Test only the first render and publish immediately.
Test a normal path and a relevant edge/failure path, and record expected versus actual behavior.
Move answer keys and private configuration into frontend code.
Replace all native browser APIs with jQuery whether needed or not.
questions.answer_key: Test a normal path and a relevant edge/failure path, and record expected versus actual behavior.
questions.explanation: Expected-versus-actual checks, relevant edge cases, and recorded limitations make the implementation easier to debug and review.
